- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Trojan War was one of the most important events in Greek mythology, fought between the Greeks and the Trojans, lasting for ten years.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The war was fought over Helen of Troy, who was the wife of Menelaus, the king of Sparta, and had been abducted by Paris, the prince of Troy.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The war was significant for honor and glory, with the Greeks fighting to uphold their honor and defend Helen's husband.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The gods and goddesses of Greek mythology were involved in the war, taking sides and participating actively.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Many of the greatest heroes of Greek mythology fought in the war, including Achilles, Odysseus, and Ajax.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Trojan War was the subject of many epic poems and stories, with the most famous being the Iliad, written by Homer.
- [USER] User inquired about which side ultimately won the Trojan War.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Greeks ultimately won the Trojan War using the Trojan Horse, a wooden horse filled with Greek warriors.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Trojan Horse was left outside the gates of Troy as a supposed offering, and the Trojans brought it inside the city.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Greek soldiers emerged from the horse at night, opened the gates of Troy, and allowed the Greek army to conquer the city.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Trojan War ended with the destruction of Troy and the death of many Trojan and Greek heroes.
- [USER] User expressed interest in the story of Helen of Troy after the war and asked if she returned to her husband.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] After the war, Helen returned to her husband, Menelaus, who was overjoyed to have her back.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In some versions of the myth, Menelaus forgave Helen for her infidelity, and they lived the rest of their lives together.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In other versions, Menelaus was angered by Helen's betrayal and almost killed her upon her return.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In most versions, Helen is reunited with Menelaus, and they return to Sparta together.
